newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Hebron gunman says he wanted to save city.
newsitem.headline: Hebron gunman says he wanted to save city.

text.p: Jewish gunman Noam Friedman said he sprayed bullets at Arab shoppers in a Hebron market on Wednesday to sabotage the handover to the PLO of the town he said was bought for the Jews 4,000 years ago by the biblical Abraham.

"Abraham bought the Cave of the Patriarchs for 400 shekels of silver. No one will return it," Friedman, triumphantly waving his fist in the air, told Israel's Channel Two television while being put into a police van after the attack.
The gunman told investigators he wanted to sabotage the handover, Israel's central area commander Major-General Uzi Dayan told army radio.

The 19-year-old off-duty soldier from Maaleh Adumim settlement near Jerusalem wounded seven Palestinians, two critically, when he indiscriminately fired his M-16 rifle into a vegetable market on Hebron's central Martyr's Street.

The Cave of the Patriarchs -- the traditional burial place of the biblical fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob and their wives -- is one reason Hebron's 400 Jews say they can lay claim to the town of 100,000 Arabs occupied by Israel in 1967.
The Bible says that in Hebron some 4,000 years ago Abraham, father of the Jews, paid the substantial sum of 400 shekels of silver for a cave in which to bury his wife Sarah.
The shooting underscored the fragility of the U.S.-sponsored Middle East peace process and the feeling of betrayal of right-wing Jews opposed to returning captured land to Arabs.

"Bibi remains alone without Jews behind him," Friedman said, using the nickname of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who is struggling to seal a deal with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to hand over 80 percent of Hebron to PLO control.
It was another religious Jew, Yigal Amir, who tried to stop land-for-peace deals by assassinating then-prime minister Yitzhak Rabin 14 months ago.

The Cave of the Patriarchs is also a holy site to Moslems, who call it the Haram al-Ibrahimi. In February 1994 Baruch Goldstein, a Jew from the nearby Kiryat Arba settlement, massacred 29 Palestinians kneeling in prayer at al-Ibrahimi mosque before survivors beat him to death.
Hebron is the last of seven West Bank towns due to be handed over to Palestinian self-rule under a 1995 Israeli-PLO interim self-rule peace accord.

The pullback, due last March, was delayed by a wave of Islamist suicide attacks in Israel ten months ago. The redeployment was further delayed by the May election of Netanyahu, who has sought to stiffen security guarantees for Hebron's Jews.
